questions.question: What purposes of evidence guide?
questions.sourceAnswer:
The evidence guide provides guidance to the interpretation and
   assessment of the unit of competency. including

   The underpinning knowledge, skills and attitude requirements for the unit
   The aspects which need to be emphasized in assessment,
   Relationships to other units, and
   The required evidence of competency.

questions.question: What role does candidate feedback play in gathering evidence?
questions.sourceAnswer:
Feedback helps candidates understand their strengths and areas for
   improvement, and it provides guidance on steps they can take to achieve
   competency.

questions.question: What role does inclusive communication play in a learning environment? provide two examples
questions.sourceAnswer:
Inclusive communication ensures that all learners clearly understand
   training and assessment requirements, feel respected, and can actively participate
   regardless of language, ability, or background.
   Examples:
   Using simple, clear language and explaining technical terms so all learners can
   understand.
   Giving instructions in multiple formats (spoken and written) to support different
   learning needs.

questions.question: What should be considered when choosing assessment methods?
questions.sourceAnswer:
Think about you own assessments and how relevant they were to:
   the skill or competency being assessed
   the purpose and nature of the assessment
   what resources are available to you and/or the candidate
   what evidence already exists in the workplace
   how easy the assessment tools are to use
   whether the method is practical in terms of time and cost
   how well it can be used to collect evidence in an integrated and realistic way
   if you need to make Reasonable adjustments for a candidate with a permanent or
   temporary disability.

questions.question: What should be done if the assessment is affecting workplace production?
questions.sourceAnswer:
If the assessment is affecting workplace production, it should be stopped
   to avoid any negative impact on the workplace operations.

questions.question: What should you know about conflict of interest? As an assessor, you will need to be aware of possible conflicts of interests and take actions to ensure that you act ethically and responsibly. Consult the NSDA Code of Conduct for Assessors.
questions.sourceAnswer:
Conflict of interest in assessments arises when an assessor’s personal
   interests, relationships, or biases compromise their ability to evaluate a
   candidate’s performance fairly and objectively. This can lead to unethical

   outcomes, damage the credibility of the assessment process, and harm
   stakeholder trust.

questions.question: What skills do we need when dealing with candidates?
questions.sourceAnswer:
Skills needed when dealing with candidates:
   • Communication skills (clear speaking, active listening)
   • Questioning skills
   • Interpersonal skills and empathy
   • Giving constructive feedback
   • Patience and respect for diversity
   • Problem solving / conflict handling
   • Maintaining confidentiality and professional ethics

questions.question: What steps should be followed in the maintenance reporting process based on an inspection report?
questions.sourceAnswer:
Record the inspection findings and identified defects; assess risk and set
   priorities; report to the authorised person; isolate or tag unsafe equipment; raise
   a maintenance request; arrange resources and corrective work; test the
   equipment after repair; document completion; and follow up unresolved issues.

questions.question: What steps should be taken actions to mitigate the action?
questions.sourceAnswer:
Actions that remove the hazard and eliminate the risk.
   Actions that replace the hazard by a less dangerous one.
   Actions that modify the product or process design.
   Actions that isolate the hazard from people.
   Actions that use engineering solutions such as a new machinery or plant.
   Actions that use administrative controls, e.g. new procedures.
   Actions that protect through personal equipment from hazards.

What strategies you should follow to ensure gender inclusivity in the training session?

questions.question: What techniques should an assessor follow when questioning a candidate?
questions.sourceAnswer:
Involve the candidate and encourage participation in the discussion.
   Avoid ambiguous, unclear, and leading questions.
   Plan the structure and order of questions before the assessment.
   Use follow-up questions to identify the range and depth of the candidate’s
   experience.
   Phrase and ask questions carefully to obtain quality information.

questions.question: What topics are included in general safety training?
questions.sourceAnswer:
Topics in general safety training:
   • Hazard identification and risk control
   • Use and care of PPE
   • Safe use of tools, machines and electricity
   • Fire safety and use of fire extinguishers
   • Emergency and evacuation procedures
   • First aid
   • Manual handling and ergonomics
   • Safety signs and symbols
   • Housekeeping
   • Reporting accidents, incidents and hazards

questions.sourceAnswer: Direct Evidence

questions.question: What type of question encourages learners to express their ideas and opinions?
questions.sourceAnswer: Open questions.

questions.question: What types of representations or materials do visual learners prefer for information?
questions.sourceAnswer:
This learning preference includes the representation of information in a

   hierarchies and other devices that instructors use to symbolize what could have
   been presented in words.

questions.question: When is oral questioning useful in assessment?
questions.sourceAnswer:
Oral questioning is useful when observation is not possible, to verify
   observations, to test underpinning knowledge, or to explore competency
   dimensions such as contingency management and problem-solving.

questions.sourceAnswer:

   Ensure that the time available to complete the assessment, while meeting
   enterprise requirements. take, account of the candidate's needs
   Have a number of shorter assessments rather than trying to cram too much into

questions.question: Which information are included in Range of variable?
questions.sourceAnswer:
The range statement also referred to as the range of variables specifies
   the range of contexts and conditions under which the competency is applicable.
   Legislation such as Occupational Safety and Health
   The range of equipment, tools, processes and procedures
   Special characteristics and needs of learners group
   Particular locations
   The range of applications arising from particular quality assurance systems

questions.question: Which information we can get from a Competency Based Curriculum Document?
questions.sourceAnswer:
A curriculum document provides the following information:
   the name and number of the Units of Competency included in the proposal
   nominal delivery hours for each unit
   a general description of the purpose of the unit of competency

Knowledge – Understanding the task or subject.
   Ability – Capacity to perform the task.

questions.question: Which types of strategies an Assessor should apply for adjusting Indigenous candidates in the assessment event?
questions.sourceAnswer:
Strategies for Indigenous candidates:
   • Respect their culture, language and beliefs.
   • Use simple language or an interpreter if needed.
   • Use oral questioning, demonstration and observation instead of written tests.
   • Be flexible with time and dates, considering cultural events and obligations.
   • Allow a support person or community member.

   • Use culturally appropriate examples and materials.

questions.question: While delivering training session what are the points you may remember when receiving feedback from the learner?
questions.sourceAnswer:
A few points to remember about:
   Thank the giver and respect their honesty and their point of view.
   Value the comments.
   Reflect on the feedback and make a decision about any follow-up action.
   If it is an important issue, act immediately, or at least set up a plan to deal with it
   Be an appropriate role model for your learners.

questions.question: While delivering training session what things you should avoid?
questions.sourceAnswer:
being poorly prepared
   Lacking variety
   Underestimating the existing skills and abilities of learners
   Using one-way communication
   Patronizing learners
   Waffling- not staying focused
   Confusing the learners
   Setting yourself up as the expert
   Not listening
   Lacking empathy
   Making assumptions
   Not starting at the level, the learner is at.
   Not having any real experience in industry.

questions.question: Who are the development partner of Bangladesh TVET system?
questions.sourceAnswer: UCEP, MAWTS, Ahshania Mission, Muslim Aids, CPD and SUF

questions.question: Who are some support persons that may assist in inclusive learning? Give examples and their roles.
questions.sourceAnswer:
Support persons assist learners to overcome barriers and participate fully
   in training and assessment.
   Examples and Roles:
   Teacher Aides / Learning Support Officers: 1. Help learners with disabilities during
   training or assessments. 2. Provide one-on-one guidance or assist with
   equipment.
   Interpreters / Translators: 1. Assist learners with limited English proficiency or
   hearing impairment. 2. Translate instructions, questions, or responses.
   Counsellors / Student Advisors: 1. Provide emotional, social, or career support. 2.
   Help learners manage stress or personal issues affecting learning.

   Mentors / Peer Support: 1. Guide learners through tasks or practical activities. 2.
   Encourage participation and build confidence.
   Family Members / Carers (where appropriate): 1. Assist with mobility,
   communication, or personal care needs during training.

questions.question: Who endorses competency standards, and why are they important in curriculum development?
questions.sourceAnswer:
Competency standards are endorsed by the relevant Industry Skills
   Council (ISC). They are important in curriculum development as they define the
   specific competencies and skills required in an industry, providing a foundation for
   designing training and assessment materials.

questions.question: Who is the responsible person for reporting in an institute?
questions.sourceAnswer:
The head of the institute (Principal) is responsible for reporting. Usually
   the designated person such as the Safety Officer / OHS officer or the supervisor
   (Head of department / Chief Instructor) receives the reports from trainers and
   staff and passes them to the Principal.

questions.question: Who must be included in the assessment process
questions.sourceAnswer:
Assessor – Conducts and evaluates the assessment.
   Candidate (Learner) – Participates in and completes the assessment.

questions.question: Why are links important in learning sessions?
questions.sourceAnswer:
Links are important in learning sessions because they help learners
   connect new information to their existing knowledge, facilitating the learning
   process.

questions.question: Why are students or trainees given vocational education and training (VET) in Bangladesh?
questions.sourceAnswer:
To gain qualifications for all types of employment, and specific skills to
   help them in the workplace. Vocational education and training is a hands-on
   approach to training. It provides accredited training in job related to technical
   skills. It involves a large number of careers and industries like trades and office
   work, retail, hospitality and technology.

questions.question: Why the authenticity of evidence is critical in the assessment?
questions.sourceAnswer:
The authenticity of evidence is critical in assessment because it ensures
   that the evidence presented truly reflects the learner's own work and abilities.
   The evidence collected from the person for assessment must be work they have
   produced or created themselves and can be directly attributed [credited] to them.

questions.question: Why do you need to review your assessment plan?
questions.sourceAnswer:
Reviewing the assessment plan is critical to ensure that the proposed
   outcomes of the assessment plan have achieved what was intended. It is normal

   to have several versions of the assessment plan before you finally reach
   agreement with your colleagues or stakeholders. However, it is important that the
   final version is communicated and confirmed with key stakeholders, and
   recorded. This can be achieved using version control.

questions.question: Why is fairness an essential assessment principle?
questions.sourceAnswer:
Fairness gives every candidate an equitable, unbiased opportunity and
   allows reasonable adjustments and appeal rights when needed, without lowering
   competency standards.

questions.question: Why is fairness an essential principle in competency-based assessment?
questions.sourceAnswer:
Fairness ensures that assessments are unbiased, accessible, and
   equitable, providing equal opportunities for all candidates to demonstrate
   competence.

questions.question: Why is it important for a TVET trainer to maintain technical competency?
questions.sourceAnswer:
They must remain current with industry technology, practices and
   standards; deliver accurate and relevant training; maintain professional
   credibility; meet competency-standard requirements; and prepare learners for
   present workplace expectations.

questions.question: Why is it important to assess all four dimensions of competency?
questions.sourceAnswer:
The dimensions of competency are important because they break down
   complex skills into specific, measurable areas. This helps organizations better
   assess and develop an individual's abilities by focusing on different aspects of a
   competency, such as knowledge, behavior, and technical skills. By understanding
   these dimensions, employers can target training, give clearer feedback, and
   ensure employees have all the skills needed to succeed in their roles. It also helps
   in fair and thorough performance evaluations and supports career growth.

questions.question: Why is it important to make reasonable adjustments in competency-based assessments?
questions.sourceAnswer:
Reasonable adjustments are designed to ascertain that all people are
   treated equally in the assessment process without compromising the integrity of
   the competency standards. These are made in the assessment process to meet
   the individual.

questions.question: Why is it important to outline specific planned responses in an Emergency Response Plan?
questions.sourceAnswer:
It ensures that individuals know how to react and what actions to take
   during different emergency situations, enhancing over all safety and
   preparedness.

questions.question: Why is it important to provide variety in the delivery of our learning sessions?
questions.sourceAnswer:
We need to provide variety in delivering sessions to:
   accommodate different learning styles (i.e. visual, auditory, reading/writing and
   kinesthetic or tactile)
   cover the different learning domains (the three Hs)
   stimulate and motivate the learners
   draw on the experiences of the learner
   keep an interesting flow (pace) happening
   Engage, Excite, Enliven.

questions.question: Why is it important to use culturally sensitive verbal and body language in an inclusive learning environment?
questions.sourceAnswer:
Using culturally sensitive language and body language is important
   because:
   1. It shows respect for learners from different backgrounds.
   2. It helps everyone feel safe, valued, and included.
   3. It prevents misunderstandings that can happen due to cultural differences.
   4. It supports better communication and builds trust.
   5. It encourages participation, especially from learners who may feel shy or
   different.

questions.question: Why is it necessary to record and report assessment outcomes?
questions.sourceAnswer:
Recording and reporting assessment outcomes ensure fairness, accuracy,
   and accountability in the assessment process. They provide evidence of learners’
   performance and progress for verification and review. These records help identify
   areas for improvement and support future training decisions. They are also
   required for institutional documentation and compliance purposes.

questions.question: Why it is important to achieve contingency management skills in CBT?
questions.sourceAnswer:
If any irregularities and breakdowns, imperfections and even unknown
   routines happens, the alternate way can help us to complete the task.

questions.question: Why it is important to maintain the principle of validity in competency based Assessment?
questions.sourceAnswer:
Validity is important because:
   • It ensures the assessment measures what it is supposed to measure (the
   required competency).
   • It makes the competency decision accurate and credible.
   • It ensures all performance criteria and evidence requirements are covered.
   • Employers and industry can trust the certificate.
   • It protects candidates from unfair decisions.

questions.question: Why maintain your equipment?
questions.sourceAnswer:
To extend the useful life of physical facilities
   To assure the operational readiness of installed equipment and maximum possible
   return on investments.
   To properly discard hazardous wastes
   To ensure the safety of personnel using the facilities, physical properties and the
   environment

questions.question: Why need RPL?
questions.sourceAnswer:
RPL (Recognition of Prior Learning) is needed because:
   • It recognises skills gained through work and life experience without formal
   training.
   • It saves time and cost by avoiding duplication of training.
   • It gives a nationally recognised certificate.
   • It improves employment and career opportunities.
   • It helps identify skill gaps for further training.

questions.question: Why need TVET data for skill development in Bangladesh?
questions.sourceAnswer:
TVET data is needed because:
   • It helps plan skills training according to labour market demand.
   • It identifies skill gaps and shortages.
   • It supports policy making and resource allocation.
   • It helps monitor quality and performance of training institutes.
   • It links training with employment (national and overseas).

questions.question: Why practice inclusivity in training and/or assessment organization?
questions.sourceAnswer:
By practice inclusivity in training and/or assessment organization can:
   Prepare its learners to work more effectively and flexibly in diverse workplaces
   and communities
   Provide more learners and clients with better quality services in an increasingly
   competitive market
   Ensure it meets its obligations arising out of legislation and standard

questions.question: Why questioning method of assessment is conducted?
questions.sourceAnswer:
Questioning is used to:
   • Assess underpinning knowledge.
   • Check understanding of procedures and reasons behind actions.
   • Assess contingency management ("what if" situations).
   • Gather supplementary evidence to support observation.
   • Help candidates with low literacy (oral questions).

questions.question: Why self-assessment for the candidates is conducted?
questions.sourceAnswer: To help candidates check their readiness for formal assessment.

questions.question: Why should assessment feedback be given promptly?
questions.sourceAnswer:
Feedback is beneficial both to the assessor and the candidate to provide
   for the following:
   review/evaluation of assessors performance
   review/evaluation of assessment process and assessment documents
   chance to explain assessment decisions made
   identifying the candidate's strengths and weaknesses
   giving guidance for further training
   encouragement of candidate who has not achieved the required level of
   competence.

questions.question: Why should an assessor assess a candidate’s contingency-management skills?
questions.sourceAnswer:
Contingency Management Skills mean the ability to respond to
   irregularities and breakdowns, imperfections and even to unknown in routines. To
   determine preparedness of a candidate to handle unexpected challenges, their
   problem-solving abilities, adaptability, decision-making skills, stress management
   capabilities, organizational skills it is important to 'assess contingency
   management skills of a candidate.

questions.question: Why should feedback be specific rather than general?
questions.sourceAnswer:
Specific feedback helps students know what they are doing well and
   what they need to improve on. Therefore, it is important to give them the most
   valuable information about their performance, rather than just general praise or
   criticism, so that their feedback is specific rather than general. And through this,
   students or employees know exactly what behavior or skill they are being
   observed for, which makes the feedback effective for them.

questions.question: Why should you give individual feedback as an assessor?
questions.sourceAnswer:
Feedback from a facilitator should focus on how a learner can improve.
   Focus on corrective actions not mistakes.
   Individual feedback from an assessor is important because it:
   Clarifies strengths and areas for improvement.
   Guides personal development with actionable insights.
   Motivates learners by recognizing progress.
   Focused, specific feedback helps learners grow effectively.

questions.question: Why we use evidence gathering tools?
questions.sourceAnswer:
Purpose of evidence gathering tools
   Help candidate understand what is expected
   Focus for the assessor in evidence gathering

   Record assessment outcome
   Identify what action is needed to address skill and knowledge gaps

questions.question: Why will you avoid Horn effect?
questions.sourceAnswer:
The horn effect causes unfair judgments because one negative trait or
   impression influences how we view someone's overall abilities or character. That’s
   why it should avoid.

questions.question: Write 2 (Two) requirements of valid evidence?
questions.sourceAnswer:
If the candidate writes any 2 of the following it should be considered as
   correct. To be considered valid, evidence must cover:
   All performance criteria and elements.
   Dimensions of competency.
   Essential skills, knowledge, and critical evidence listed in the evidence guide.
   All "musts" specified in the range statement.
   The candidate may write the answer in paragraph form instead of using bullet
   points; it should still be considered correct. It may be: The evidence must cover all
   aspect of UoC/CS or, it covers assessment requirements.

questions.question: Write the 3 (three) key points of time management skills?
questions.sourceAnswer:
If the candidate writes any 3 of the following it should be considered as
   correct. The key points of time management skills are as below:
   ability to meet time-based requirements and deadlines
   ability to identify and adjust high and low priority tasks
   ability to use time effectively (i.e. prevent irrelevant issues or distractions from

questions.question: Write down the dimensions of competency? Describe with example.
questions.sourceAnswer:
There are four dimensions of competency.
   Task skills - Task skills require performance of the tasks according to the set
   standard as described in the unit of competency and expected in the workplace.
   Task skills are usually described in the elements and performance criteria.
   Task management skills - It involves carrying out tasks simultaneously or
   managing multiple tasks at the same time. Task management skills are found in
   the performance criteria, underpinning skills and knowledge. They may also
   appear in the rage statements.
   Contingency management skills - It mean the ability to respond irregularities and
   breakdowns, imperfections and even to unknown in routines. Contingency
   management skills are found in the critical aspects of evidence, performance
   criteria and underpinning knowledge. They also appear in the rage statements.
   Job/Role environment skills - It is the capacity to work with others and adapt to
   different situations is central to successful performance. They are covered in the
   key competencies and underpinning skills and knowledge.
   Example: Let us consider a job of a Photocopy Machine Operator:
   Task Skills: Use a photocopier
   Task management skills: Select the right paper and functions
   Contingency management skills: Clear paper jams
   Job/Role environment skills: Liaise with team members on print / job
   requirements

study.answer: The four dimensions are task skills, task management skills, contingency management skills, and job/role environment skills.

questions.question: Write down the rules of evidence.
questions.sourceAnswer:
Validity: The assessor is assured that the learner has the skills, knowledge
   and attributes as described in the module or unit of competency and associated
   assessment requirements. For example, the evidence will not be valid if you
   instruct a candidate to solve printer problems by simply asking: Type a standard
   office memo on a word processor.
   Validity is assured when the performance required matches the performance
   described in a competency standard.
   Currency: The assessor is assured that the assessment evidence demonstrates
   current competency. This requires the assessment evidence to be from the
   present or the very recent past.

   Currency means evidence needs to be checked to ensure it shows recent
   performance.
   Sufficiency: The assessor is assured that the quality, quantity and relevance of the
   assessment evidence enables a judgement to be made of a learner’s competency.
   A judgement has to be made concerning how much evidence to call for. How
   much is required for the assessor to accept the performance as competent? Too
   little evidence risks the assessment not being reliable; too much leads to waste of
   time and effort.
   Tell your candidates that the evidence they present for RPL should be organised
   and presented in a format that makes it easy for the assessor to make a
   judgement of competence.
   Authenticity: The assessor is assured that the evidence presented for assessment
   is the learner’s own work.
   Authenticity means evidence needs to be checked to ensure it actually relates to
   the performance of the person being assessed, and not that of another person.
   Checking for authenticity is important when some supplementary sources of
   evidence are used in assessment.
   Consistentency: Does the evidence show that the candidate consistently meets
   the standards under workplace conditions? Does the evidence incorporate
   multiple items of evidence?
   Recent -Is the evidence less than five years old?
questions.reviewNote: মূল PDF-এ অতিরিক্ত “Consistency” এবং “less than five years” লেখা আছে। নির্দিষ্ট ৫ বছরের নিয়ম ধরে মুখস্থ করবেন না। এই অ্যাপের CBLM-ভিত্তিক Rules of Evidence টপিকের সঙ্গে মিলিয়ে পড়ুন।

questions.question: Write some principles of competency based assessment
questions.sourceAnswer:
Validity - Assessments are valid when they assess what they claim to
   assess.
   Reliability - Assessments are reliable when the methods and procedures used are
   consistently interpreted and applied over time with different candidates,
   assessors and in various situations.
   Flexibility - Assessments are flexible when they are appropriate to the range of
   knowledge, skills and attitudes encompassed by competency standards, the range
   of delivery modes and locations as well as the needs of a wide range of
   candidates.
   Fairness - Assessments are fair when they are accessible to all eligible candidates
   regardless of age, gender, disability, ethnic or social background, language
   barriers or geographic location, and when no one is disadvantaged by the
   procedures or methods used.

study.answer: The four assessment principles are Validity, Reliability, Flexibility and Fairness.
study.bn: সঠিক দক্ষতা যাচাই, একই মানে বিচার, উপযুক্ত পদ্ধতি, সবার ন্যায্য সুযোগ।
study.example: কম ইংরেজি জানা প্রার্থীকে অনুমোদিত ভাষা-সহায়তা দিন; কাজের মান কমাবেন না।

questions.question: Write the stages of preparing an assessment plan.
questions.sourceAnswer:
The stages of preparing an assessment plan is given bellow:
   1. Read and understand the unit of competency
   2. Select an element or elements
   3. Identify evidence requirements
   performance criteria
   dimensions of competence
   underpinning skills and knowledge
   critical aspects of competence
   4. Identify best ways of collecting evidence- refer to Rules of Evidence
   5. Document assessment/evidence plan

study.answer: Understand the unit of competency, select the elements, identify evidence requirements, choose suitable evidence-gathering methods, then document the assessment plan.
study.bn: Unit বুঝি → element বাছি → কী প্রমাণ চাই ঠিক করি → কীভাবে নেব ঠিক করি → plan লিখি।
study.example: কম্পিউটার ব্যবহারের unit পড়ে প্রয়োজনীয় কাজ ও checklist ঠিক করে সময়, জায়গা ও পদ্ধতি plan-এ লিখুন।

questions.question: Write the steps of organizing and conducting a competency based assessment in the correct order.
questions.sourceAnswer:
Plan and prepare the assessment (plan, tools, resources, venue)
    Brief the candidate: explain the process, get consent and check readiness
    Conduct the assessment and gather evidence
    Make the assessment decision (competent / not yet competent) against the
    criteria
    Record the assessment results
    Provide feedback to the candidate
    Report the results and review the assessment process

study.answer: Plan and prepare; brief the candidate; collect evidence; make a decision; record results; give feedback; report and review.
study.bn: প্রস্তুতি → বুঝিয়ে বলা → প্রমাণ → সিদ্ধান্ত → লিখে রাখা → feedback → review।
study.example: মেশিন চালাতে দেখে checklist পূরণ করুন, মানের সঙ্গে মিলিয়ে সিদ্ধান্ত দিন ও উন্নতির কথা বলুন।

questions.question: Write the types of hazards with examples?
questions.sourceAnswer:
Physical Hazards: Examples are unguarded machine parts like saw blades,
   constant noise, prolonged exposure to sun or cold.

   Biological Hazards: Examples include blood, viruses and animal and bird
   droppings.
   Chemical Hazards: Examples are cleaning products, pesticides and gasoline.
   Ergonomic Hazards: Examples are poor lighting, workstations that are too high or
   low for you or a job that requires you to repeat the same movement over and
   over.

questions.question: You have to keep the workplace as safe as possible. In that case how can you identify hazards of your workplace?
questions.sourceAnswer:
I can identify hazards through methods such as:
   Reviewing illness and injuries
   Conducting workplace inspections or safety audits, and
   When a hazard is reported by someone at the workplace
   OR
   Past incidents and accidents
   Input by employees
   Examining workplaces or work areas
   Review of safety instruction for equipment and materials
   Any kind of creative thinking such as brainstorming
   Advice from legislation, standards, checklists or external consultants.
